title: Short Stirling LK276 (Little Easton)
memorial_details: A large freestanding stone with a bronze plaque stands in the gardens at Easton Lodge, Little Easton. The IWM register records the stone and plaque in good condition. It does not state who made the stone or when it was dedicated, and the site is Grade II listed.
inscription: IN LOVING MEMORY OF THE CREW OF/ STIRLING BOMBER, L.K.276, 190 SQD/ NEWTON FIELD, GREAT DUNMOW/ 21ST NOVEMBER 1944/ FG OFF J I KIDGELL RAAF/ FG OFF W W D'A BRAIN RNZAF/ FG OFF E D WOODS/ SGT H HOLT/ FLT SGT R D PAYNE/ FLT SGT R M DAUNCEY/ FLT SGT A G REID/ PER ARDUA AD ASTRA

sources.title: Flight Sergeant A G Reid and crew of Short Stirling LK276 (WMR 97190)
20/21.11.1944 190 Squadron Stirling IV LK276 Fg Off Kidgell, Great Dunmow, Newton Field, Essex

narrative:
Stirling IV LK276 of 190 Squadron flew from Great Dunmow (Newton Field) on a night glider-towing sortie on 20/21 November 1944. It was towing Horsa glider P-F573 with Flying Officer Brain aboard as check pilot. The glider was released at 21:08 and landed safely. At 21:13 the pilot asked to land and was told to hold off and circle the outer perimeter lights. At 21:20 the Stirling hit willow trees and high-tension cables, skidded along a bank and exploded. All seven crew died. Local reporting places the impact in the field where Great Dunmow Primary School now stands.

The cause is disputed. Aircrew Remembered says the board of enquiry blamed the pilot for failing to monitor his altimeter, and also reports later investigations that a Luftwaffe night fighter shot the aircraft down. The rafweb casualty listing says it may have been shot down by an enemy intruder. The bench plaques for Dauncey, Woods and Holt say the crash was the result of enemy action; that is the plaque wording, not a verified finding.

The seven crew were Flying Officer James Ian Kidgell (pilot, RAAF, 23), Flying Officer William Walter D'Arcy Brain (second pilot and instructor, RNZAF, 26), Flying Officer Ernest Douglas Woods (navigator, 26), Sergeant Hugh Holt (flight engineer, 20), Flight Sergeant Ronald David Payne (air bomber, 21), Flight Sergeant Reginald Matthew Dauncey (wireless operator and air gunner, 23) and Flight Sergeant Arthur George Reid (air gunner, 33). Kidgell, Brain and Reid are buried at Brookwood Military Cemetery; Woods at Chapeltown, Holt at Burnley, Payne at Lewisham and Dauncey at Northwich.

external_narratives.summary: Casualty listing for 190 Sqn Stirling IV LK276 giving all seven crew with rank, service number, age, service and burial cemetery. Says the aircraft may have been shot down by an enemy intruder.
key_details: All seven crew listed with service numbers and ages

external_narratives.summary: Register entry for the Reid bench: a plaque on a cast iron and wooden bench with Great Dunmow Town Council crests on the ends. Dedication listed as 2007, with a note that the Dunmow Broadcast describes benches dedicated on 21 November 2010. Erector and maintainer not stated.
key_details: Seat, Woodlands Park Drive, Great Dunmow, CM6 1ZR
Erected by / maintained by not stated

external_narratives.summary: Register entry for the stone with bronze plaque at Easton Lodge, Little Easton, naming seven crew. Maker, dedication date and maintainer are not stated. Links the seven Great Dunmow benches as erected by Great Dunmow Town Council.
key_details: Stone of remembrance, Easton Park Gardens, Easton Lodge, CM6 2BB

external_narratives.summary: Loss page for Stirling IV LK276 with a timed account of the night glider-towing sortie, both versions of the cause, and a crew table with ages, service numbers and burial places. Notes the seven commemorative seats in Great Dunmow and the 21 November 2010 ceremony.
key_details: Board of enquiry blamed pilot (altimeter); later reports of a night fighter
Crew table: ranks, ages, service numbers, burials
Page is internally inconsistent: says six killed at scene and rear gunner died of injuries, yet lists seven dead

external_narratives.summary: Bench plaque for Kidgell on Woodlands Walk. Dedication field says 2000, which conflicts with the 2010 newspaper account. Lists CWGC ID 2667301.
Bench plaque for Dauncey at Newton Green, dedicated 21 November 2010 by Canon David Ainge. Plaque says the crash was as the result of enemy action.
Bench plaque for Woods on Stortford Road, dedicated 21 November 2010. Plaque says enemy action.
Bench plaque for Holt at Threaders Green, dedicated 21 November 2010. The first plaque gave his age as 33; a replacement with the correct age of 20 was fitted in March 2011.

memorial_address: Easton Park Gardens, Easton Lodge, Little Easton, Uttlesford, Essex, CM6 2BB
community_connection: Great Dunmow Town Council erected seven benches in the town, one for each crew member, and the final ceremony was held on 21 November 2010, with relatives attending. The sources read do not say who looks after the Little Easton stone.
